title: News
about: Collocations for talking about the news: how a story breaks, leaks out and hits the headlines, and the typical language of news reports, such as hold talks, launch a campaign, keep sb informed and no loss of life.

parts.title: Common mistakes
parts.note: Найчастіша пастка юніту: «останні новини» — the latest news, а не the last news. Last — «останній за порядком», після якого вже нічого не буде, тому the last news — хіба що «остання звістка» перед довгою тишею: The last news we had from him was a postcard in May. І пам'ятай: news — незлічуване й завжди в однині: the news is good, a piece of news, а не a news чи the news are.

rows: What's the latest news? / What's the latest?
an interesting piece of news / news item
on the first page of the paper
on the front page of the paper

items.pattern: a (news) story breaks · break – broke – broken · breaking news
items.meaning: a piece of news becomes public for the first time
items.example: The **story** about the new motorway **broke** on a Monday, and by Tuesday the whole village had signed a petition.
more: Journalists were outside the footballer's house an hour after the **story broke**.
**Breaking news**: the bridge on the ring road has been closed after a lorry crash.
items.watchOut: Про новину, що стала відомою, кажуть the story broke, без out. Break out — спалахнути (про війну, пожежу, епідемію): A fire broke out. Breaking news — термінова новина, «екстрене повідомлення».

items.pattern: news comes in (of / about sth) · news has just come in · news is coming in
items.meaning: new information reaches a newspaper, TV or radio station
items.example: **News is coming in** of heavy snow on the roads north of Manchester.
more: **News has just come in** that tonight's concert in the park has been cancelled because of the wind.
We sat by the radio all night as **news came in** from the flooded villages.
items.watchOut: News — однина: news is coming in, а не news are coming in. «Надходять новини» у випусках новин — саме come in; news arrives теж можливо, але звучить книжніше.

items.pattern: news / details / the truth leaks out · news of sth leaks out · leak sth (to the press)
items.meaning: secret information becomes known, although someone wanted to keep it secret
items.example: **News** of the price rise **leaked out** a week before the company announced it.
more: We wanted Mum's party to be a surprise, but somehow **the news leaked out**.
Somebody **leaked** the plans for the new stadium to the local paper.
items.watchOut: «Новина просочилася» — leaked out, а не flowed out чи ran out (run out — закінчитися). У розмові ще кажуть the news got out.

items.pattern: hit the headlines · hit – hit – hit · also make / grab the headlines
items.meaning: suddenly become an important story in the news
items.uk: потрапити в заголовки газет, стати головною новиною
items.example: Our little village **hit the headlines** when a farmer found a box of Roman coins in his field.
more: The bakery **hit the headlines** after it baked a cake as tall as a bus.
Food prices have **hit the headlines** again this week.
items.watchOut: «Потрапити в заголовки» — hit the headlines, а не get into / fall into the headlines. Тут з the, а hit у минулому часі теж hit.

items.pattern: make (the) headlines · make headlines around the world / across the country
items.meaning: be reported a lot in the news because it is surprising or important
items.example: Last summer's record heatwave **made headlines** around the world.
more: A grandmother who passed her driving test at 85 **made the headlines** in the local paper.
Small towns rarely **make headlines** unless something strange happens.
items.watchOut: Make headlines, а не do / create headlines. Можна з артиклем і без: make headlines, make the headlines.

items.pattern: the front-page headline · on the front page · a front-page story / photo
items.meaning: the biggest headline, on the first page of a newspaper
items.example: Grandad still has the newspaper from the day he was born: the **front-page headline** was about a heatwave.
more: The weekly paper's **front-page headline** was about our school's win in the national choir competition.
The **front-page headline** was huge: 'WE DID IT!'
items.watchOut: Перша сторінка газети — the front page, а не the first page. Тому front-page headline, front-page news. Перед іменником — з дефісом: a front-page story, але on the front page.

items.pattern: the latest news (on / about / from sth) · the latest (informal)
items.meaning: the most recent news
items.example: What's **the latest news** about the train strike?
more: I always check **the latest news** on the weather before we go walking in the hills.
We're still waiting for **the latest news** from the vet about our cat.
items.watchOut: «Останні новини» — the latest news, а не the last news. The last news — це «остання звістка», після якої новин уже не було: The last news we had from him was a postcard in May. І news — однина: the latest news is good.

items.pattern: be / become headline / front-page news · no a: news is uncountable
items.meaning: be such an important story that it is in big headlines or on the front page
items.uk: бути головною новиною, бути на першій шпальті
items.example: A missing cat isn't usually **headline news**, but this one walked 200 miles home.
more: The floods **were front-page news** for a whole week.
When the old pier fell into the sea, it **was headline news** all over the country.
items.watchOut: Headline news і front-page news — без a: news незлічуване. Не first-page news і не title news: заголовок — headline, а title — назва книжки, фільму чи пісні.

items.pattern: an item of news · a news item · also a piece of news, a news story
items.meaning: one single report or story in the news
items.example: There was a short **news item** about our school concert on the local radio.
more: The last **item of news** was about a dog that can surf.
I read an interesting **news item** about cheap train tickets for students.
items.watchOut: News — незлічуване: не a news і не two news. Одна новина — a piece / an item of news, a news item або a news story.

items.pattern: run a story (about / on sth) · run – ran – run · also carry / publish / print a story
items.meaning: publish a story in a newspaper or magazine, or show it on the news
items.example: Our street party was so popular that the local paper **ran a story** on it the next week.
more: Several magazines **ran stories** about the singer's new house.
The evening news **ran a story** on rising food prices.
items.watchOut: Run тут — «опублікувати, дати в номер», а не «бігти». Кажуть run / carry / publish a story. Make up a story — вигадати історію, це інше.

items.pattern: flick through a newspaper / magazine / book · also flip / leaf through
items.meaning: turn the pages quickly and look at them without reading carefully
items.example: I **flicked through the newspaper** while the kettle was boiling.
more: Dad **flicks through the paper** over breakfast and only reads the sport.
She **flicked through** a holiday brochure and chose Crete in five minutes.
items.watchOut: «Гортати» — flick / flip / leaf through, обов'язково з through. Не list (це «список») і не turn the newspaper. Read the newspaper — читати уважно, flick through — швидко переглядати.

items.pattern: give (sb) the go-ahead (to / for sth) · get / receive the go-ahead · also give the green light
items.meaning: give official permission for something to start
items.example: The council has **given the go-ahead** for a new swimming pool in the park.
more: We finally **got the go-ahead** from our landlord to paint the kitchen.
Once the doctor **gives you the go-ahead**, you can start running again.
items.watchOut: «Дати зелене світло» — give the go-ahead (з the і через дефіс) або give the green light. Не give the permit: permit — документ, перепустка.

items.pattern: a surprising / unexpected / dramatic turn of events · in a … turn of events
items.meaning: a change in what is happening, usually one that nobody expected
items.example: In a dramatic **turn of events**, the team at the bottom of the league beat the champions 3–0.
more: The rain stopped just as the wedding started: a lucky **turn of events** for everyone.
After a strange **turn of events**, our lost dog turned up at the police station.
items.watchOut: Поворот подій — a turn of events: turn, а не turning, і events завжди в множині. Часто з in: in an unexpected turn of events.

items.pattern: (all) interested parties · party = a person or group in an agreement or argument
items.meaning: people or groups who are connected with a situation and affected by it
items.example: The plans for the new market are online, and all **interested parties** can comment until May.
more: Shop owners, residents and other **interested parties** met at the town hall to discuss the parking problem.
The plans were sent to all **interested parties**, including local shops and the bus company.
items.watchOut: «Зацікавлені сторони» — interested parties, а не interested sides. Party тут — сторона в угоді чи суперечці, а не вечірка чи партія. І не interesting parties: interesting — «цікавий».

items.pattern: hold talks (with sb / about sth) · hold – held – held · peace talks
items.meaning: meet officially to discuss something and try to agree
items.example: The football club and the council will **hold talks** next week about building a new stadium.
more: Residents **held talks** with the council about the noise from the motorway.
Teachers and the government are **holding talks** to try to end the strike.
items.watchOut: «Проводити переговори» — hold talks, а не spend talks (spend — проводити час) і не make talks. Переговори — talks, у множині.

items.pattern: outline plans / proposals / ideas (for sth / to do sth)
items.meaning: describe the main points of a plan, without the details
items.uk: окреслити плани, представити в загальних рисах
items.example: The mayor **outlined plans** for a new park where the old factory used to be.
more: At the meeting, the head teacher **outlined her plans** for a longer school day.
The travel company **outlined plans** to add more flights to Greece next summer.
items.watchOut: Outline — окреслити в загальних рисах, без деталей. Не contour plans. Draw up plans — складати детальний план, це вже наступний крок.

items.pattern: launch a campaign (to do sth / against sth) · an anti-smoking / road safety campaign
items.meaning: start an organised series of activities to achieve something
items.example: The town has **launched a campaign** to keep the beaches free of litter.
more: Parents **launched a campaign** to save the village school.
The police are **launching a road safety campaign** before the summer holidays.
items.watchOut: «Запустити кампанію» — launch a campaign; можна й start a campaign, а run a campaign — проводити її. Campaign читається /kæmˈpeɪn/, g не вимовляється. Не плутай з company — компанія, фірма.

items.pattern: the top job (at / in sth) · get / take over / quit the top job
items.meaning: the most important position in an organisation
items.example: The **top job** at the town museum is going to a 32-year-old historian.
more: Who will take over the **top job** at the football club next season?
He gave up the **top job** at a big bank to open a small café by the sea.
items.watchOut: «Найвища посада» — the top job, а не the high job чи the upper job. Main job — основна робота (на відміну від підробітку), це інше.

items.pattern: attract (a lot of / sb's) attention · attract attention with / over sth
items.meaning: make people notice and become interested in someone or something
items.example: The bright pink house on the corner **attracts attention** from everyone who walks past.
more: The singer **attracted a lot of attention** with her unusual dress.
A man shouting on his phone **attracted attention** from everyone on the bus.
items.watchOut: «Привернути увагу» — attract / draw / catch attention, а не involve attention: involve — залучати когось до справи. Pay attention — звертати увагу самому, а attract attention — коли увагу звертають на тебе.

items.pattern: a controversial decision / plan / issue · controversy (noun)
items.meaning: a decision that many people disagree with and argue about
items.example: The council's **controversial decision** to turn the old park into a car park led to protests.
more: Fans are still arguing about the referee's **controversial decision** in the last minute.
Raising ticket prices was a **controversial decision**, but the club needed the money.
items.watchOut: «Суперечливе рішення» (про яке сперечаються) — controversial, а не contradictory: contradictory — той, що сам собі суперечить (contradictory statements). Рішення — decision, а solution — розв'язання проблеми. Наголос: con-tro-VER-sial.

items.pattern: take sb hostage / captive · be taken hostage / captive · hold sb hostage
items.meaning: catch someone and keep them as a prisoner, often to get something in return
items.uk: взяти когось у заручники / в полон
items.example: In the novel, a family on a sailing holiday **are taken hostage** by smugglers.
more: Two sailors were **taken captive** by pirates, but they were freed a week later.
In the TV series, robbers **take a whole train full of passengers hostage**.
items.watchOut: «Взяти в заручники» — take sb hostage, без in і без a: не take in hostages. Тримати в заручниках — hold sb hostage. Hostage читається /ˈhɒstɪdʒ/: наприкінці «-ідж», а не «-ейдж».

items.pattern: seize control of sth · also take / gain control of sth
items.meaning: take control of something suddenly, often by force
items.example: In the second half, the home team **seized control of** the game and scored three goals.
more: As soon as Dad fell asleep, my sister **seized control of** the TV remote.
In the film, a gang of thieves **seizes control of** a cruise ship.
items.watchOut: Seize читається /siːz/, як «сіз». «Захопити контроль» — seize / take control of, а не catch control. Після control — of: control of the airport.

items.pattern: lose control (of sth) · lose – lost – lost · be out of control
items.meaning: no longer be able to control or manage something
items.example: I **lost control** of my bike on the wet leaves and fell off.
more: The supply teacher completely **lost control** of the class on her first day.
The pilot **lost control** of the small plane for a moment, but landed safely.
items.watchOut: Втратити — lose /luːz/, а не loose /luːs/ («вільний, розхитаний»). Не miss control: miss — пропустити або сумувати. Після control — of: lose control of the car.

items.pattern: keep a close watch on sb/sth · also keep a close eye on sb/sth
items.meaning: watch someone or something carefully, especially to check for problems
items.example: Farmers are **keeping a close watch on** the river after a week of heavy rain.
more: **Keep a close watch on** the kids when they're near the pool.
We're **keeping a close watch on** prices before we book our holiday.
items.watchOut: «Пильно стежити» — keep a close watch on, а не a near watch (near — поруч у просторі) і не keep a close look. Прийменник — on. Розмовне — keep a close eye on.

items.pattern: keep sb informed (of / about sth) · also keep sb posted / up to date
items.meaning: keep telling someone the latest information
items.example: Please **keep me informed** about your plans for Saturday.
more: The airline **kept passengers informed** about the delay by text.
I'll **keep you posted** when I hear from the estate agent.
items.watchOut: «Тримати в курсі» — keep sb informed / posted / up to date, а не keep sb in course. Після keep sb — дієприкметник informed, не informing.

items.pattern: as the news / story / situation develops
items.meaning: as more things happen and more information becomes known
items.example: We'll bring you more on the flooding in the valley **as the news develops**.
more: Check the website for updates **as the story develops**.
The airport will post new flight times **as the situation develops**.
items.watchOut: «У міру розвитку подій» — as the news / the story / the situation develops. News — однина: as the news develops, не develop.

items.pattern: talks break down · break – broke – broken · a breakdown in talks
items.meaning: discussions end without any agreement
items.example: **Talks** between the teachers and the government **broke down** after just an hour.
more: The bus strike began after **talks** with the company **broke down**.
**Talks** about the price of the house **broke down**, so we started looking elsewhere.
items.watchOut: «Переговори зірвалися» — talks broke down. Не broke out: break out — спалахнути (війна, пожежа). Talks — у множині: the talks have broken down.

items.pattern: sth catches fire · catch – caught – caught · compare: set fire to sth
items.meaning: start burning
items.example: A tea towel **caught fire** when I left it too close to the cooker.
more: The barbecue **caught fire** and burnt half the fence.
Dry grass **catches fire** very easily in summer.
items.watchOut: «Загорітися» — catch fire, без артикля. Не get fire. Set fire to sth — підпалити щось: Someone set fire to the bins.

items.pattern: lightning strikes (sth) · strike – struck – struck · be struck by lightning
items.meaning: lightning hits something
items.example: **Lightning struck** the old oak tree in our garden during the storm.
more: Our TV stopped working after **lightning struck** the house.
My uncle's barn was **struck by lightning** last summer.
items.watchOut: Блискавка — lightning, без e. Lightening — «світлішання», lighting — освітлення. «Влучила блискавка» — lightning struck або hit, а не beat. Пасив: was struck by lightning.

items.pattern: there was no loss of life · loss of life (uncountable) · no lives were lost
items.meaning: nobody was killed
items.example: The fire destroyed three shops, but luckily there was **no loss of life**.
more: The floods damaged hundreds of homes, but there was **no loss of life**.
The storm brought down trees all over town, but there was **no loss of life**.
items.watchOut: «Без людських жертв» — there was no loss of life, а не no human victims. Loss of life — в однині й без артикля. Lose — втратити (дієслово), loss — втрата (іменник).

warmup.q: And now for the ___ sports news.
warmup.explain: Останні (найсвіжіші) новини — the latest news. The last news — «остання звістка», після якої нічого не було.

warmup.uk: Заголовок на першій шпальті сьогоднішньої газети — про новий міст.
warmup.q: Today's ___ headline is about the new bridge.
warmup.explain: Перша сторінка газети — the front page, тому front-page headline.

warmup.uk: Наша футбольна команда потрапила в заголовки газет.
warmup.explain: Потрапити в заголовки — hit (або make) the headlines.

warmup.uk: У місцевій газеті є цікава новина про наш парк.
warmup.q: There's an interesting ___ about our park in the local paper.
warmup.explain: News — незлічуване, тому не a news. Одна новина — a news item, an item / a piece of news.

warmup.uk: Уряд зустрінеться з усіма зацікавленими сторонами.
warmup.q: The government will meet all the interested ___.
warmup.explain: Зацікавлені сторони — interested parties. Party тут — сторона в угоді чи суперечці.

warmup.uk: Профспілка і компанія проведуть переговори в понеділок.
warmup.q: The union and the company will ___ talks on Monday.
warmup.explain: Проводити переговори — hold talks. Spend — проводити час.
Тримати в курсі — keep sb informed (або posted). In course — калька.

warmup.uk: Сухе листя в саду загорілося від багаття.
warmup.q: The dry leaves in the garden ___ fire from the bonfire.
warmup.explain: Загорітися — catch fire. Set fire to sth — підпалити щось.

A.q: Do you know the ___ news about the school trip? Is it still on?
A.explain: Останні (найсвіжіші) новини — the latest news. The last news — «остання звістка», після якої новин не було.

A.q: Somebody must have talked: news of the café's new menu ___ out a week before the launch.
Grandpa reads every page, but my sister only ___ through the paper to find the horoscopes.
A.explain: Гортати газету — flick through the paper. List — складати список.

B.q: The decision to build flats on the old football ground was very ___.
B.explain: Суперечливе рішення, про яке сперечаються, — controversial. Contradictory — той, що сам собі суперечить.

B.q: The horse suddenly ran off, and the young rider ___ control.
B.explain: Втратити контроль — lose control. Miss — пропустити; loose — вільний, розхитаний.

B.q: The talks between the dockers and the port owners broke ___, so the strike will go on.
B.explain: Переговори зірвалися — talks broke down. Break out — спалахнути (про війну, пожежу).

example.title: Our town in the news
example.uk:
Минулого літа наше тихе містечко потрапило в заголовки газет. Одного вечора налетіла сильна гроза, і блискавка влучила в старий вітряк на пагорбі. Дах загорівся, але пожежники приїхали швидко, і, на щастя, обійшлося без людських жертв.

Про це стало відомо тієї ж ночі, і невдовзі з усього міста почали надходити новини: повалені дерева, перекриті дороги, немає світла. Місцеве радіо пообіцяло тримати всіх у курсі в міру розвитку подій.

Наступного ранку на першій шпальті місцевої газети був заголовок «ВІТРЯК У ВОГНІ». Навіть тато, який зазвичай лише гортає газету, прочитав усе до останнього слова. Через місяць міська рада дала зелене світло на відбудову вітряка.
example.en:
Last summer our quiet little town [[hit the headlines|a4]]. One evening a huge storm arrived, and [[lightning struck|b18]] the old windmill on the hill. The roof [[caught fire|b17]], but the fire brigade came quickly, and luckily there was [[no loss of life|b19]].

The [[story broke|a1]] that same night, and soon [[news was coming in|a2]] from all over town: trees down, roads closed, no electricity. The local radio promised to [[keep everyone informed|b14]] [[as the news developed|b15]].

The next morning, 'WINDMILL IN FLAMES' was the [[front-page headline|a6]] in the local paper. Even Dad, who usually just [[flicks through the paper|a11]], read every word. A month later, the council [[gave the go-ahead|b1]] to rebuild the windmill.
